info.title: Ambivo Procurement API
info.description:
**Ambivo Procurement** is the buy side: somebody asks to buy something, a
budget holder approves it, a buyer turns approved requests into orders
against vendors, the goods arrive, and the vendor's bill is matched against
what was ordered and what was received before anyone pays it.

It runs inside the Ambivo Core API (`ingress.ambivo.com`) and shares its
auth, tenancy, access control and response envelope. There is no separate
Procurement service.

## The chain

```
purchase_requisition  ──►  purchase_order  ──►  goods_receipt  ──►  Bill
   (what we need)          (what we agreed)     (what arrived)    (what we owe)
                \                                    /
                 └──────  three-way match  ─────────┘
```

## The entities

| Entity | What one record is |
|---|---|
| `purchase_requisition` | An internal request to buy. Header only. |
| `purchase_requisition_line` | One requested item, and how much of it has been ordered. Its own collection. |
| `purchase_order` | The commitment to a vendor. Also a blanket agreement or a release against one. |
| `goods_receipt` | One delivery against one order. Posting it moves stock. |
| `goods_receipt_line` | One received line of a receipt. A posted line is never edited. |
| `goods_receipt_event` | What happened to a line: received, accepted, rejected, delivered_to_stock, cancelled, closed_short, reopened, corrected. Append-only. |
| `vendor_price_agreement` | A negotiated price for a vendor and a product, for a period. |
| `bill` | The vendor's invoice. Belongs to Ambivo Books; see that spec. |

**Vendors are not an entity.** A vendor is an `account` with
`relationship_type='vendor'`. Managing vendors and supplier relationships is
the ordinary CRM account and contact machinery.

## Four rules that shape the whole API

**Requisition lines are their own collection, and that is load-bearing.**
The buyer's work list is "which requested LINES are still unordered" across
every open request in the tenant, and one requested line can end up on
several purchase orders. Both are queries over lines; neither is expressible
as an array on a header.

**Quantity roll-ups are written by the server.** A requisition line
refuses `ordered_qty`, `received_qty` and `open_qty` on PATCH
(`READ_ONLY_FIELD_<FIELD>`). A purchase order line refuses `received_qty`,
`billed_qty`, `rejected_qty` and `closed_qty` when the value sent differs
from the stored one (`PURCHASE_ORDER_LINE_READ_ONLY_FIELD_<FIELD>`). A
blanket's `released_amount`, `remaining_amount` and `release_count` are
recomputed from its releases each time a release is drawn or the blanket
is recomputed.

**A blanket agreement is approved once; its releases are not.** Drawing an
agreed quantity inside the agreed term is fulfilment, not new spend. A
release outside the term, or one past the committed value, does go through
approval — and the response says which and why.

**Posting is separate from recording, and stricter.** A goods receipt is
written in `draft` while somebody counts what came off the van, and posted
when they are satisfied. Only posting moves stock. Recording asks for `C`;
posting asks for `D`.

## Which company's books (multi-entity)

"Entity" in Ambivo Books means a **legal company**, not the platform's
`entity_type`. Requisitions, price agreements and purchase orders carry
`books_entity_id`. On create it is resolved server-side in this order:

1. `books_entity_id` on the request body.
2. The company mapped to the record's `site_code` in the tenant's site list.
3. Blank, which means the tenant's default company.

A client does not need to send it. A value that is not all digits is
refused with `INVALID_BOOKS_ENTITY_ID`. `POST /user/purchase_order` and
`PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}` refuse it with a different code; see
`POST /user/purchase_order`. Core cannot check that the company
exists. A goods receipt copies `books_entity_id` from its order.

## Money

Every monetary field carries an FX block: `currency`, `fx_rate`,
`base_<field>`, `fx_pending`. **Aggregate the `base_` field, never the
native one** — summing a native amount across currencies produces a number
that is not money. Consolidating requisition lines into an order never mixes
currencies or companies for the same reason.

## Response envelope

Success and refusal both return HTTP 200 with a `result` field. `1` is
success, `2` is failure, and a failure carries `error_code`. Branch on
`result` and `error_code`. Two cases use the HTTP status: a missing or
expired token gets HTTP 401 with no body. A tenant whose account review is
pending gets HTTP 403. Every route makes that account check.

```json
{ "result": 2, "error_code": "PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED",
  "error": { "message": "Could not read this record. Try again." },
  "status_code": 200, "request_path": "/user/purchase_order/66e3f0c1a2b4c5d6e7f80911" }
```

A read that fails answers `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`. An empty list always means
there are no rows. A detail read answers `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED` before it
answers `NOT_FOUND`. An unexpected failure answers `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

A collection path with no handler for the verb, such as
`GET /user/purchase_requisition`, answers HTTP 405. Use the `/list` route.

## Gates

Most services check `module_access` for the module named on each operation
(`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_<MODULE>`). Tenant admins pass. Most writes also need
the tenant to be entitled to `procurement` (`PROCUREMENT_REQUIRES_PRO`).
Creating or updating a purchase order needs `books` (`BOOKS_REQUIRES_PRO`).

## Record ids on reads

List and single-record reads that go through the platform's entity reader
return the stored document. Its id is `id`, with no named id beside it.
Fields computed by the record's serializer (`is_editable`, `comments_count`
and similar) are absent. A linked record can be attached next to its id
field, for example `account` beside `account_id` or `user` beside `userid`.
It holds that record's export fields.
Create and update responses return the serialized record, which carries the
named id (`purchase_requisition_id`, `goods_receipt_id` and so on) and an
`id` copy.

## Pagination, filtering and sorting

List endpoints take `page_num` (1-based, default 1) and `page_size` (default
50, at most 500) as query arguments. They reply with `total_count`,
`page_num` and `page_size`. The rows skipped are `(page_num - 1) * page_size`.
`page` and `limit` are the old names. They are still read for inventory
mobile <= 1.1.0 and are deprecated (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2).

Lists also take `match_filter_dict` (a JSON object), `search_text`,
`sort_dict` (JSON), `get_count` and `ids_list` (a JSON array). The two dicts
travel JSON-encoded because a GET has no body. `ids_list` narrows a read to
named ids and is ANDed onto `match_filter_dict`, never merged.

The work lists and audit lists (`open_lines`, `expected_deliveries`,
`goods_receipt_line/list`, `goods_receipt_event/list`) accept only the
`match_filter_dict` keys listed on each route. Any other key is refused with
`MATCH_FILTER_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED_<FIELD>`. The top-level filter arguments they
took before still work for one release and are deprecated.

On the entity-reader lists (requisitions, requisition lines, price
agreements, purchase orders, blankets, goods receipts and the dock's
expected deliveries), `total_count` is counted on page 1 only. Later pages
report `0`.

On those lists and single-record reads, a tenant admin is scoped by owner
and `access_dict` like any other caller. The dock's expected deliveries list
is scoped by site instead.

## Dropdowns (picklists)

Every dropdown uses `GET /entity/data?entity_type=<type>&action=picklist`,
with `match_filter_dict`, `search_text`, `sort_dict`, `page_num` and
`page_size` (default 1000, at most 1000). The endpoint is documented in the
CRM spec under Entity Data.

These four types are read through their own service. The caller needs `R`
on the module (`purchase_order` for orders). Without it the answer is the
service's `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_<MODULE>` code with the message "You cannot
view this list." `tenant_scope` is ignored. A failed read answers
`PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`. To look up rows by id, send
`match_filter_dict={"_id": {"$in": ["<hex id>", ...]}}`. Each id may also be
written `"ObjectId('<hex id>')"`. Each row carries
`name` and `<entity_type>_id`. `name` joins these parts with ` · ` and skips
blank ones:

| entity_type | `name` is built from |
|---|---|
| `purchase_order` | the order's own `name` |
| `purchase_requisition` | `requisition_number`, `name` |
| `vendor_price_agreement` | `agreement_number` (or `name`), product name (or SKU) |
| `goods_receipt` | `receipt_number`, `po_number`, `receipt_date` |

The rows are under `data.<entity_type>`, or under `data.values` when
`use_native=false`. `purchase_order` rows are always under `data.values`.

## Deprecated routes

These still work exactly as before for one release. Each call writes a
DEPRECATED line to the server log. They are marked `deprecated` below.

| Deprecated | Use |
|---|---|
| `POST /user/purchase_order/manage` `action: add` | `POST /user/purchase_order` |
| `action: get` with an id | `GET /user/purchase_order/{id}` |
| `action: get` or `get_entity_ids` | `GET /user/purchase_order/list` |
| `action: update` | `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}` (to send for approval, `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/submit`) |
| `action: delete` | `DELETE /user/purchase_order/{id}` or `DELETE /user/purchase_order?ids_list=[...]` |
| `action: get_kanban` | `GET /user/purchase_order/kanban` |
| `POST /user/purchase_order/approve` | `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}/approval` |
| `POST /user/purchase_order/create_bill` | `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/bill` |
| `POST /user/purchase_order/create_from_installed_base` | `POST /user/installed_base/{id}/purchase_order` |
| `POST` and `GET /user/purchase_order/picklist` | `GET /entity/data?entity_type=purchase_order&action=picklist` |
| `POST /user/purchase_order/approval_chain` | `GET` and `PUT /user/purchase_order/approval_chain` |

`POST /user/purchase_order/search` was removed on 2026-09-26.

Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition`. Rows are scoped by owner and

200.description:
A failed read returns `result: 2` with `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`,
never an empty list.

post.summary: Create a requisition
post.description:
Opens in `draft` with `approval_status: not_required` and a
`requisition_number` of `PR-NNNNNN`. `line_list` (or `lines`) in the
body creates its lines. Needs `C` on `purchase_requisition`.

The seeded `basic` role grants `C`, `R` and `U` on
`purchase_requisition` and `purchase_requisition_line`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `NAME_REQUIRED` | `name` is blank |
| `INVALID_PRIORITY` | `priority` is not in the list |
| `LINE_NEEDS_PRODUCT_OR_DESCRIPTION` | a line has neither |
| `LINE_QTY_NOT_A_NUMBER`, `LINE_QTY_MUST_BE_POSITIVE` | a line's `qty` |
| `INVALID_PRODUCT_ID`, `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` | a line's `product_id` |
| `PURCHASE_REQUISITION_DATE_INVALID` | `needed_by_date` cannot be read as a date |
| `INVALID_BOOKS_ENTITY_ID` | `books_entity_id` is not all digits |
| `SITE_CODE_NOT_REGISTERED` | `site_code` is not a site the tenant has registered. `data` is `{site_code}`. |

`INVALID_BOOKS_ENTITY_ID` carries a message that says what to fix.

**`warnings`.** The response has a `warnings` list only when the
`books_entity_id` sent differs from the company of the requisition's
site. This can be an intercompany transfer, so the requisition is saved
with the company sent. The message is: "Site {site_code} belongs to
another company. This was saved with the company you chose. Check that
is intended, for example an intercompany transfer."

warnings.description: Present only when the company sent is not the company of the site. The requisition is saved as sent.

delete.description:
Deletes the named requisitions that are in `draft`, and their lines.
Other ids are counted in `refused`. Needs `D` on `purchase_requisition`.
The seeded `basic` role has no `D`.

When none of the ids is a draft the call fails with
`ONLY_DRAFT_REQUISITIONS_CAN_BE_DELETED`. No ids gives `INVALID_DATA`.
A malformed id gives `INVALID_PURCHASE_REQUISITION_ID`.

refused.description: Named ids that were not deleted. They were not drafts, or not found in the tenant.

get.description:
Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition`. The stored document, scoped by
owner and `access_dict`. Its id is `id`. `NOT_FOUND` when the caller
cannot see it.

patch.summary: Edit a draft or rejected requisition
patch.description:
**Only a `draft` or `rejected` request is editable**, and anything else
is refused with `REQUISITION_NOT_EDITABLE_IN_STAGE_<STAGE>`. Needs `U`
on `purchase_requisition`.

`line_list` (or `lines`) REPLACES the lines wholesale when it is a list.
An empty `line_list` leaves the lines unchanged.

These keys are refused with `IMMUTABLE_FIELD_<FIELD>`:
`purchase_requisition_id`, `tenant_id`, `site_code`,
`requisition_number`, `line_count`, `estimated_total`,
`base_estimated_total`, `qty_ordered_pct`, `approval_status`,
`approval_steps`, `current_approval_seq`, `created_by_userid`,
`timestamp`. `stage` is ignored.

post.summary: Send for approval
post.description:
Needs `U` on `purchase_requisition`. Only a `draft` or `rejected`
request can be submitted (`REQUISITION_NOT_SUBMITTABLE_IN_STAGE_<STAGE>`),
and it needs at least one line (`REQUISITION_HAS_NO_LINES`).

Clears any earlier approval steps, builds the chain, and gates the
request on its first pending step (`stage: pending_approval`). The
approvers of that step get a notification.

**Submit sets the stage.** A `rejected` request moves to
`pending_approval` and can be decided again through
`PATCH /user/purchase_requisition/{id}/approval`. Submit also clears
`approved_by_userid`, `approved_ts`, `approval_notes`,
`approval_steps` and `current_approval_seq`.

The stage change is added to `comments` as a `status_change` entry. For a
request that was rejected, the entry names who rejected it and the notes
they left.

**Amount-banded routing.** `purchase_requisition_settings_dict.approval_threshold_list`
holds bands of `{label, min_amount, max_amount, approval_chain_userids}`.
The band is matched on `base_estimated_total` (the FX-normalised total).
Of the bands that contain the amount, the one with the highest
`min_amount` wins. A `max_amount` of `0` has no upper bound. With no
matching band, the tenant's default chain is used. The default chain is
also used when nobody in the band's chain is above the creator.

Approvers are the chain members above the creator, one step each, or the
whole chain when the creator is not in it. When nobody is above the
creator, the tenant admins other than the creator share one step.

The request goes straight to `approved` when no step results: no
default chain to fall back to, a creator who is a tenant admin at the top
of the chain, or no other admin to escalate to.

patch.description:
`decision` is trimmed and lower-cased. Anything other than `approved`
or `rejected` gives `INVALID_DATA`.

**The creator cannot approve their own request**
(`SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED`); tenant admins override. On a sequenced
chain the caller must be an approver on the CURRENT step
(`NOT_AN_APPROVER`), or a tenant admin. Approving moves to the next
pending step and notifies its approvers. The request is `approved` once
every step has approved. Any rejection rejects the whole request
immediately.

With no steps, the decision sets `approval_status` and `stage` directly.

**Needs `U` on `purchase_requisition`**
(`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PURCHASE_REQUISITION`, "You cannot approve or reject a
purchase requisition. Ask an administrator for access."). `U` is the same
privilege that updates, submits and cancels a request. Tenant admins pass.
The privilege is checked **before the request is read**. The refusal is the
same whether or not the id exists. The request is then loaded within the
tenant, as update and cancel load it.

**Only a request in `pending_approval` can be decided.** Any other stage
gets `PURCHASE_REQUISITION_NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL`, "This purchase
requisition is not waiting for approval." Purchase orders follow the same
rule through `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}/approval`, with
`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL`.

**A decision moves the request's lines with it.** Every line gets the
request's new `requisition_stage` and `requisition_number`, and its
`is_buyer_actionable` is recomputed.

An approved request turns the flag on for its lines that still owe a
quantity: `status` is `open` or `partially_ordered`, and `open_qty` is above
0. It turns the flag off on the rest. A rejected request turns it off on
every line. A step that leaves the request in `pending_approval` writes that
stage again and turns the flag off.

So the lines of a request approved here appear on
`GET /user/procurement/open_lines`, and
`POST /user/purchase_order/from_requisitions` accepts them.

The line write runs after the decision is saved. A failure to write the
lines is logged and leaves the decision standing. Such lines are repaired
by the next recompute of the request, for example when one of its lines is
closed short.

`already: true` comes back, with nothing written, for a decision on a
sequenced request that is already approved or rejected and whose stage
still says so. With no steps it comes back only for approving a request
that is already approved.
`PURCHASE_REQUISITION_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS` when the id is not in the
tenant.

200.description: The requisition's fields sit at the top level of the envelope.

post.summary: Withdraw a request
post.description:
Refused once anything has been ordered against it
(`REQUISITION_ALREADY_ORDERED`, when `qty_ordered_pct` is above 0).
Needs `U` on `purchase_requisition`. No stage is checked.

Sets `stage: cancelled` and marks every line `cancelled`. A `reason` is
appended to `notes`.

post.summary: Raise requisitions from Inventory's reorder suggestions
post.description:
The join between the two apps. Inventory computes `reorder_due` and
`suggested_order_qty` on every stock row; without this that is a list
somebody reads on one screen and retypes into another.

**One requisition PER SITE, returned as a list.** `site_code` is an
access-control code, not a label: a single requisition spanning two
sites would be visible to staff scoped to either, and approvable by
somebody with authority over half of it.

**It skips, it does not refuse.** A stale id, another tenant's row, a
malformed id, or a row whose suggestion has since gone to zero comes
back in `skipped` with a reason. Failing the whole call over one row
means the person re-picks all of them.

**The stored `suggested_order_qty` is read, never recomputed here.**
Recomputing would be a second implementation of the reorder rule, and
the buyer would be shown a different number from the Inventory screen
they just left. It is already net of `qty_on_order`.

When the stock row has a `preferred_vendor_id`, the line gets that
vendor as `suggested_vendor_account_id` and is priced through the same
rules as `GET /user/procurement/price`. A price above zero sets
`estimated_unit_price` and `price_basis`. Otherwise the price stays at
zero and the line is still created.

Needs `C` on `purchase_requisition`. Each requisition is created as by
`POST /user/purchase_requisition`, in `draft`. `inventory_item_id_list`
is required (`INVENTORY_ITEM_ID_LIST_REQUIRED`) and holds at most 500
ids (`TOO_MANY_INVENTORY_ITEMS`).

200.description: The requisitions created, and what was skipped.

purchase_requisition_list.description: One entry per site. Each entry is `{purchase_requisition: {...}}`.

skipped.description:
Rows that produced no line. Reported rather than
silently dropped.

get.summary: Requisitions grouped by stage, for a board
get.description:
The board builder purchase orders use (`GET /user/purchase_order/kanban`). Rows are scoped by owner, `access_dict` and the
caller's role rollup. Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition`.

`tenant_scope` is not accepted: the board never drops the per-record access
filter. A `stage` key inside `match_filter_dict` is ignored; use `stages`.

Columns are the eight requisition stages plus any other `stage` value
found in the caller's records. Custom stages are not merged in, so
`stage_meta` is null. Cards are newest first. A malformed `last_id` gives
`INVALID_LAST_ID`.

A tenant admin sees every requisition on the board. Each card is the
serialized record, with `purchase_requisition_id`, `id`, `is_editable`
and `is_buyer_actionable`.

parameters.name: stages
parameters.description: JSON list of the columns to return. Default all.

parameters.name: stage
parameters.description: Load more of this one column, with `last_id`.

get.summary: Read the tenant's default approval chain
get.description:
An ordered list of userids, ascending authority, from
`purchase_requisition_settings_dict.approval_chain_userids`. Any tenant
user may read it. No module privilege is checked.

put.description:
**Tenant admins only** (`ADMIN_REQUIRED`). The body is the WHOLE chain:
sending a shorter one removes approvers. Blank and repeated ids are
dropped, keeping the first. Every id must be a user in the tenant
(`APPROVER_NOT_IN_TENANT`). A value that is not a list gives
`INVALID_PAYLOAD`. A missing or empty value clears the chain. Requests
already submitted keep their steps.

updated.description: 1 when the tenant record changed, 0 when the chain was already this.

get.description:
Filter by `requisition_id` for the lines of one request. Needs `R` on
`purchase_requisition_line`. Rows are scoped by owner and `access_dict`.

Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition_line`. The stored document; its id is
`id`. `NOT_FOUND` when the caller cannot see it.

patch.description:
Needs `U` on `purchase_requisition_line`. The line's requisition must be
`draft` or `rejected` (`REQUISITION_NOT_EDITABLE_IN_STAGE_<STAGE>`).

These keys are REFUSED with `READ_ONLY_FIELD_<FIELD>`: `ordered_qty`,
`received_qty`, `open_qty`, `requisition_id`, `tenant_id`, `line_num`
and `base_estimated_amount`. The same line checks as on create apply,
and the requisition's totals are recomputed.

post.summary: Stop ordering against a line short of the full quantity
post.description:
**A reason is required** (`CLOSE_SHORT_REASON_REQUIRED`). Without one
the requester has no way to find out what happened to their request, and
it is indistinguishable from a mistake.

Needs `U` on `purchase_requisition_line`. No stage or status is checked.
Sets `status: closed_short`, `open_qty: 0` and
`is_buyer_actionable: false`, and recomputes the requisition. An
`approved`, `partially_ordered` or `ordered` requisition with nothing
left outstanding and a closed-short line becomes `closed`.

get.summary: The KPI header — open demand, approvals, commitment and leakage
get.description:
⭐ **A tile that could not be computed comes back as `null`, not `0`.**
"We do not know" and "there are none" are different facts, and showing the
second when the first is true is how a buyer concludes there is nothing to
do.

This is only the header. The saved boards underneath come from the shared
dashboard collection, not from here.

Needs `R` on `purchase_order`. Every tile counts the whole tenant, with
no per-record access filter. Money tiles sum the `base_` field, falling
back to the native field per document.

awaiting_my_approval.description: Pending requisitions with a pending step that names the caller.

committed_open.description: `base_total_amount` of purchase orders in `approved` or `ordered`, blankets excluded.

received_not_billed.description: `base_total_received_amount` of posted goods receipts whose order has no `bill_id`.

agreements_expiring.description: Active price agreements with a `valid_to_date` above 0 and no later than `expiring_window_days` from now. Dates already past are counted.

get.description:
The same list contract as every other procurement record: `page_num`,
`page_size`, `get_count`, `match_filter_dict`, `sort_dict`, `search_text`,
`ids_list`, `list_id`. Default page size 50, at most 500.

The same read as `GET /user/purchase_order/{id}` and the deprecated
`POST /user/purchase_order/manage` `action: get`, so record access (owner
and `access_dict`) is identical on all three. No module privilege is
checked.

This is not the receiving dock's list. The dock reads
`GET /user/procurement/expected_deliveries`, which carries no prices.

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description: A saved list to apply (static ids or a dynamic filter).

200.description:
A failed read is reported as a failure (`error_code:
PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`), never as an empty list.

post.summary: Create a purchase order
post.description:
The body is the order: `name`, `account_id` (the vendor), `po_line_list`,
`stage` and the rest. A `payload` wrapper is unwrapped. `purchase_order_id`
and `tenant_id` in the body are ignored. No module privilege is checked.

`stage` may be `draft` (the default when blank), `pending_approval` or
`cancelled`. `pending_approval` builds the approval chain. The save rules
and refusal codes are the same as `action: add` on the deprecated
`POST /user/purchase_order/manage`, listed there.

A `books_entity_id` that is not all digits gives
`BOOKS_ENTITY_ID_MUST_BE_THE_NUMERIC_ID_OF_AN_AMBIVO_BOOKS_COMPANY_OR_OMITTED_TO_USE_THIS_TENANTS_DEFAULT`.
A tenant without `books` gets `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

**`data.warnings`.** It is present only when the `books_entity_id` sent
differs from the company of the order's site. The order is saved with the
company sent.

delete.description:
Deletes each id in `ids_list`. A non-admin deletes only orders they own.

patch.description:
The body is the fields to change. A `payload` wrapper is unwrapped. The
caller must own the order, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a tenant
admin (`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`).

A save cannot set a stage an action owns. `approved` and `rejected` come
from `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}/approval`, `received` from a goods
receipt, and `billed` from `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/bill`. To send
a draft for approval, use `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/submit`. The
save rules and refusal codes are the same as `action: update` on the
deprecated `POST /user/purchase_order/manage`, listed there.

put.description: The same body, answer and refusals as PATCH.

delete.description: A non-admin deletes only orders they own.

200.description: `{result: 1, data: [{deleted, purchase_order_id}]}`. A list, as the batch delete answers.

post.summary: Send a purchase order for approval
post.description:
No body. Sets `stage: pending_approval` and `approval_status: pending`,
through the same save as `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}`. The server
builds the approval chain and notifies the approvers of the first step.

Resubmitting a rejected or approved order starts its approval over.
An order that has received goods or has a bill cannot be sent for
approval again (`PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_NOT_SETTABLE`, `data.reason`
`received` or `billed`). The caller must own the order, hold `U` in its
`access_dict`, or be a tenant admin (`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`).

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Submitted", data: {...the order: stage, approval_status, approval_steps, current_approval_seq}}`

patch.summary: Approve or reject one purchase order
patch.description:
`decision` is trimmed and lower-cased. Anything other than `approved` or
`rejected` gives `INVALID_DATA` with the message "Choose approved or
rejected." `comment` is saved as the approval notes. `notes` is accepted
in its place. This mirrors `PATCH /user/purchase_requisition/{id}/approval`.

Acts on the order's **current step**, so the caller does not name a
step. The caller must be an approver on that step (`NOT_AN_APPROVER`) or
a tenant admin. With no steps, the decision sets `approval_status` and
`stage` directly. Approving moves to the next pending step and notifies
its approvers. Any rejection rejects the order.

The creator cannot approve their own order (`SELF_APPROVAL_NOT_ALLOWED`).
Tenant admins override.

**Needs `U` on `purchase_order`** (`NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_PURCHASE_ORDER`, "You
cannot approve or reject a purchase order. Ask an administrator for
access."). Tenant admins pass. The privilege is checked **before the order
is read**. The refusal is the same whether or not the id exists. A grant in
the order's `access_dict` is not authority to decide it.

The caller must then own the order, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a
tenant admin (`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`).

**Only an order in `pending_approval` can be decided.** Any other stage gets
`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_AWAITING_APPROVAL`, "This purchase order is not waiting
for approval." An approved order's remaining quantities go on order in
Inventory.

`already: true` comes back, with nothing written, for a decision on a
sequenced order that is already approved or rejected. With no steps it
comes back only for approving an order that is already approved.

data.description: The order, plus the decision fields.

post.summary: Raise the vendor bill for a purchase order
post.description:
Builds a Bill from the order: one line per order line, the order's
total, `site_code`, `books_entity_id` and currency, and `doc_num`
`BILL-NNNNNN`. The order moves to `billed`, and the three-way match is
recorded on it (`match_status`, `billed_amount`, each line's
`billed_qty`). The match never refuses the bill.

The caller must own the order, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a
tenant admin. No module privilege is checked.

**Idempotent.** An order that already has a bill returns that bill with
`already: true` and `created: 0`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS` | not found, or no write access |
| `BLANKET_PURCHASE_ORDER_IS_NOT_BILLABLE` | the order is a blanket |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_BILLABLE` | the order is `rejected` or `cancelled` |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_APPROVED` | the order is not `approved`, `ordered`, `received` or `billed` |
| `BILL_CREATE_FAILED` | a concurrent create collided and no bill could be adopted |

stage.description: Stage to create the bill in. A value that is not a Bill stage becomes `draft`.

200.description: `{result: 1, message: "Created", data}`. `data` is as on the deprecated `POST /user/purchase_order/create_bill`.

post.summary: Raise a draft renewal order for an installed-base record
post.description:
No body. The on-demand twin of the nightly sweep's PO creation. The
record must be `direction='purchased'` (`INSTALLED_BASE_NOT_PURCHASED`).

**Idempotent.** When `meta.renewal_purchase_order_id` on the record names
an order that still exists, the answer is
`{purchase_order_id, installed_base_id, already: true, created: 0}`.
Otherwise a `draft` order is created for the record's counterparty, and
its id is written to that marker.

The caller must own the record, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a
tenant admin (`INSTALLED_BASE_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`). No module
privilege is checked. A tenant without `books` gets `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

post.summary: List, create, update or delete purchase orders
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use the verb routes: `POST /user/purchase_order`,
`GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /user/purchase_order/{id}`,
`GET /user/purchase_order/list` and `GET /user/purchase_order/kanban`.

One POST carries an `action`. Each action calls the same service method as
its verb route, so the save rules below apply to both.

`get_kanban` returns the same records grouped into stage buckets for a board.

No module privilege is checked on any action. `action` is lower-cased; an
unknown one gives `UNSUPPORTED_ACTION`. On `get`, a failed read answers
`PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`. An unknown id on `get` answers an empty list.

| action | What it does | Response |
|---|---|---|
| `get`, `get_entity_ids` | With `purchase_order_id`, that one order. Otherwise a page, scoped by owner and `access_dict`. `ids_list` narrows the page and is AND-ed with `match_filter_dict`. `page_size` defaults to 50 and is not capped. | `purchase_order` (array of stored documents, id in `id`), `total_count`, and `page_num`, `page_size` on a page |
| `get_kanban` | Orders grouped by `stage`, including the tenant's custom purchase order stages. Takes `items_per_stage` (1 to 50, default 10), `stages`, `stage`, `last_id`, `match_filter_dict`, `search_text`. A `tenant_scope` sent by the caller is ignored: record access always applies. | `data.kanban.<stage>` with `purchase_orders`, `total`, `has_more`, `last_id`; `data.stage_order`, `data.stage_meta`, `data.group_by`, `data.total_count`; `msg_list` |
| `add` | Creates an order from `payload`. `stage: pending_approval` builds the approval chain. | `data`: the order plus `created: 1`, and `data.warnings` when the company differs from the site's company |
| `update` | Updates `purchase_order_id` from `payload`. The caller must own the order, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a tenant admin (`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`). | `data`: the order plus `updated` |
| `delete` | Deletes `purchase_order_id`, or each id in `ids_list` / `purchase_order_ids`. A non-admin deletes only orders they own. | `data`: a list of `{deleted, purchase_order_id}` |

`update` refuses a line's `received_qty`, `billed_qty`, `rejected_qty` or
`closed_qty` when it differs from the stored value
(`PURCHASE_ORDER_LINE_READ_ONLY_FIELD_<FIELD>`). Removing a line that has
received, billed or closed quantity gives
`PURCHASE_ORDER_LINE_HAS_RECEIPTS`. An invalid `stage`, `approval_status`
or `po_type` gives `PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_INVALID`,
`PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVAL_STATUS_INVALID` or `PURCHASE_ORDER_TYPE_INVALID`.
`update` and `delete` without an id give `MISSING_PURCHASE_ORDER_ID`.

**A save cannot set a stage an action owns.** `add` may open an order
in `draft`, `pending_approval` or `cancelled`. `update` may move it to
those, and from `approved` to `ordered`. `approved` and `rejected` come
from `PATCH /user/purchase_order/{id}/approval`, `received` from a goods
receipt, and `billed` from `POST /user/purchase_order/{id}/bill`. A
stage sent back exactly as stored is not a change. A blank `stage` on
`update` is refused; on `add` it means `draft`. Nor may `update` record
an approval decision: an `approval_status` other than `pending`,
`pending` on an order that is not left in `draft` or `pending_approval`,
or an approval step marked decided, is refused. The approval chain
(`approval_steps`, `current_approval_seq`, `approver_userids`) and
`stage_before_received` belong to the server: a save that changes the
chain is refused, and `stage_before_received` is ignored. Nothing is
written when a save is refused.

An order that has received any goods, or has a bill (`bill_id` or
`is_bill_interfaced`), never goes back to `draft` or `pending_approval`,
even after it is cancelled. `data.reason` is `received` or `billed`.

Moving an order back to `draft`, or resubmitting a rejected or approved
order to `pending_approval`, starts its approval over: every step goes
back to pending and a multi-step chain starts again from step one.

A save that newly references a requisition line (every reference on
`add`, only the ids an `update` introduces) is refused when the caller
may not order against it (not a tenant admin and no `U` on
`purchase_requisition_line`), or when the line cannot be ordered (closed
or cancelled, or its requisition is not `approved` or
`partially_ordered`). `data.requisition_lines` lists each line, with a
`reason` for a line that cannot be ordered.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_NOT_SETTABLE` | the save sets `approved`, `rejected`, `received` or `billed`, or `ordered` from anything but `approved`, or moves an order that has received goods or has a bill back to `draft` or `pending_approval`. `data: {requested, current, reason?}` |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_INVALID` | a blank `stage` on `update`, or an unknown stage |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVAL_STATUS_NOT_SETTABLE` | `approval_status` other than `pending`, `pending` on an order not left in `draft` or `pending_approval`, or a step marked decided. `data: {requested, current}` |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_APPROVAL_CHAIN_NOT_SETTABLE` | the save changes `approval_steps`, `current_approval_seq` or `approver_userids` (on `add`, any non-empty value). `data: {requested: <field>}` |

Messages a person reads, by case: "Use Approve to approve a purchase
order.", "Use Reject to reject a purchase order.", "Record a goods
receipt to receive a purchase order.", "Create the bill to bill a
purchase order.", "Use Approve or Reject to record an approval
decision.", "Approvers come from the approval chain in settings.",
"This purchase order has received goods, so it cannot go back to
draft." (or "has a bill", or "cannot be sent for approval again").
| `REQUISITION_LINE_ORDER_NOT_ALLOWED` | a newly referenced requisition line the caller may not order against |
| `REQUISITION_LINE_NOT_ORDERABLE` | a newly referenced requisition line that cannot be ordered |

On `add` and `update`, a tenant without `books` gets `INTERNAL_ERROR`
from this route. A `books_entity_id` on `add` that is not all digits gives
`BOOKS_ENTITY_ID_MUST_BE_THE_NUMERIC_ID_OF_AN_AMBIVO_BOOKS_COMPANY_OR_OMITTED_TO_USE_THIS_TENANTS_DEFAULT`.

**`data.warnings` on `add`.** It is present only when the
`books_entity_id` sent differs from the company of the order's site.
This can be an intercompany transfer, so the order is saved with the
company sent. The message is: "Site {site_code} belongs to another
company. This was saved with the company you chose. Check that is
intended, for example an intercompany transfer."

post.summary: Raise a draft renewal order for an installed-base record
post.description:
Deprecated. Kept for inventory mobile <= 1.1.0 (RETIRE-AFTER-INVENTORY-MOBILE-1.2). Use `POST /user/installed_base/{id}/purchase_order`. Same rules and answer.

The on-demand twin of the nightly sweep's PO creation. The sweep only fires
inside the notice window and only when the record requires a purchase order;
this raises one when a person asks.

⚠ The record must be `direction='purchased'` (`INSTALLED_BASE_NOT_PURCHASED`).

**Idempotent.** When `meta.renewal_purchase_order_id` on the record names
an order that still exists, the response is
`{purchase_order_id, installed_base_id, already: true, created: 0}`.
Otherwise a `draft` order is created for the record's counterparty, and
its id is written to that marker.

The caller must own the record, hold `U` in its `access_dict`, or be a
tenant admin (`INSTALLED_BASE_NOT_FOUND_OR_NO_ACCESS`). No module
privilege is checked. `MISSING_INSTALLED_BASE_ID` (this route only) and
`INVALID_INSTALLED_BASE_ID` cover a missing or malformed id. A tenant
without `books` gets `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

data.description: The new order's fields plus `installed_base_id` and `created`, or the idempotent answer.

get.summary: Approved demand not yet on an order
get.description:
**The buyer's screen, and what consolidation is performed from.**
Sorted by `needed_by_date` ascending, with a `by_vendor` roll-up. Within
a page, lines with no date move to the end.

Only lines with `is_buyer_actionable: true` appear: the request is
`approved` or `partially_ordered`, the line is `open` or
`partially_ordered`, and something is still unordered.

Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition_line`. Every such line in the tenant
is listed, with no per-record access filter.

`by_vendor` covers the lines on this page, largest first. Its totals sum
`base_estimated_amount` (the FX-normalised amount), or `estimated_amount`
where that is empty.

**Filters.** `match_filter_dict` narrows the list and is AND-ed onto it.
Keys: `suggested_vendor_account_id` (or `vendor_account_id`),
`deliver_to_site_code` (or `site_code`), `books_entity_id`,
`needed_by_date`, `needed_by_before` (epoch seconds; lines with no date
are left out), `product_id`, `requisition_id`, `requester_userid`,
`currency`. The vendor, site and company keys take equality only.
Operators: `$in`, `$nin`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`,
`$exists`. Sort fields: `needed_by_date`, `requisition_number`,
`product_name`, `suggested_vendor_account_id`, `_id`.

Refusals: `MATCH_FILTER_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED_<FIELD>`,
`MATCH_FILTER_OPERATOR_NOT_ALLOWED_<OP>`, `INVALID_MATCH_FILTER_DICT`,
`SORT_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED_<FIELD>`, `INVALID_SORT_DICT`, `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Rows per page. Above 500 is treated as 500.

200.description: Outstanding lines, and a per-vendor roll-up.

by_vendor.description: Advisory grouping. The buyer chooses the vendor at order time.

post.summary: What orders WOULD be created
post.description:
Creates nothing. A buyer selecting thirty lines needs to see they are
about to raise four orders and against which suppliers, before
committing.

A POST despite being a read, because the input is a list of ids that can
run to hundreds. It has no side effects.

Needs `R` on `purchase_requisition_line`. Reads `requisition_line_ids`
and `vendor_account_id` only. It refuses the same lines
`POST /user/purchase_order/from_requisitions` refuses.
`estimated_total` sums the lines' `estimated_amount` in full, at the
requester's estimate.

200.description: The grouping that would be applied.

post.summary: Consolidate requisition lines into purchase orders
post.description:
**One order per (vendor, currency, legal company, site).** Every term is
load-bearing:

- one order goes to one supplier;
- one order is invoiced in one currency;
- one order is ONE COMPANY'S liability — an order spanning two
  companies cannot produce a correct bill for either;
- `site_code` is an access-control code, so merging two branches makes a
  document neither branch's staff can fully see.

**Splitting is the same call.** `quantities` part-orders a line and the
remainder stays on the work list. Asking for more than remains is
CAPPED, not refused: a buyer ordering a vendor's pack size should not
have to edit somebody else's requisition to do it.

Each line is priced through the rules of `GET /user/procurement/price`
(an agreement, or the product's cost). When nothing is found the
requester's `estimated_unit_price` is used. The PO line's `price_basis`
records which, with `requisition_estimate` for the estimate.

Needs `C` on `purchase_order` and `U` on `purchase_requisition_line`.
Each order is created as by `POST /user/purchase_order`
`action: add`, with `data_source: requisition`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `REQUISITION_LINE_IDS_REQUIRED` | no ids |
| `INVALID_PURCHASE_REQUISITION_LINE_ID` | an id is malformed |
| `REQUISITION_LINE_NOT_FOUND_<id>` | an id is not in the tenant |
| `REQUISITION_NOT_APPROVED_<id>` | the request stage copied onto the line (`requisition_stage`) is not `approved` or `partially_ordered` |
| `REQUISITION_LINE_NOT_OUTSTANDING_<id>` | the line is not `open` or `partially_ordered` |
| `REQUISITION_LINE_FULLY_ORDERED_<id>` | nothing remains on the line |
| `NO_VENDOR_FOR_LINE_<id>` | no `vendor_account_id` and no suggested vendor |
| `INVALID_QTY_FOR_LINE_<id>`, `QTY_MUST_BE_POSITIVE_<id>` | a `quantities` entry |
| `NO_ORDERABLE_LINES` | nothing was left to order |
| `CONSOLIDATION_STAGE_NOT_ALLOWED` | `stage` is not `draft` or `pending_approval` |

A refusal from the purchase order service answers that service's code.
For example, an invalid `stage` gives `PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_INVALID`. A
tenant without `books` gets `BOOKS_REQUIRES_PRO`.

**The orders are created first and the roll-up applied second, with no
transaction across them.** The response reports `orders_created`,
`lines_applied` and `rollup_failed` so a partial outcome is stated
rather than inferred from the absence of an error.

rollup_failed.description:
True when the orders exist but the requisition roll-up
failed. The demand still reads as outstanding, which
is visible on the work list.

get.description:
Blankets only. A list mixing an agreement with the releases drawn from

onto `match_filter_dict`.

Needs `R` on `purchase_order`. Rows are scoped by owner and

200.description: Blanket agreements. A failed read gives `PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED`.

get.summary: An agreement, its releases, and what is left of it
get.description:
Needs `R` on `purchase_order`. Tenant-scoped, with no per-record access
filter. Releases are every order with this `blanket_po_id`, by
`release_seq`, rejected and cancelled ones included.
`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND` or `PURCHASE_ORDER_IS_NOT_A_BLANKET` when the
id does not name a blanket.

post.summary: Draw a release against a blanket
post.description:
**A release inside the agreed term and inside the committed value opens
`ordered` WITHOUT its own approval.** The commitment was approved when
the blanket was, and that is the point of the instrument.

One that falls outside either opens `pending_approval`, and
`needs_approval_reason` says which:
`OUTSIDE_AGREEMENT_TERM`, `EXCEEDS_COMMITTED_AMOUNT` or
`COMMITMENT_UNREADABLE`. The term is `agreement_start_date` to
`agreement_end_date`, where `0` is open. The ceiling is
`committed_amount * (1 + purchase_order_settings_dict.blanket_over_commit_tolerance_pct / 100)`.
The tolerance defaults to **zero**. A blanket with no `committed_amount`
has no ceiling.

Omitting `lines` draws the next scheduled tranche of each line's
`release_schedule`, or everything still undrawn. A quantity above what a
line has left is capped. Releases are priced from the blanket's own
lines, never re-resolved from current vendor rates.

The release is created as by `POST /user/purchase_order`
`action: add`, with `po_type: release`, the blanket's vendor, site and
company, and `notes` as its `description`. The blanket's drawdown is
then recomputed. Needs `C` on `purchase_order`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND`, `PURCHASE_ORDER_IS_NOT_A_BLANKET` | the id does not name a blanket |
| `BLANKET_NOT_APPROVED` | `approval_status` is not `approved` or `not_required` |
| `BLANKET_IS_CLOSED` | the blanket is `rejected` or `cancelled` |
| `BLANKET_LINE_NOT_FOUND_<id>` | a `lines` entry matches no blanket line |
| `BLANKET_LINE_FULLY_RELEASED_<line_id>` | nothing is left on that line |
| `INVALID_QTY_FOR_BLANKET_LINE_<line_id>`, `QTY_MUST_BE_POSITIVE_<line_id>` | a `qty` |
| `NOTHING_LEFT_TO_RELEASE` | nothing to draw |

A refusal from the purchase order service answers that service's code.

line_id.description: The blanket line to draw on.

release_date.description: Epoch seconds. Defaults to now. Checked against the term, and used as `po_date`.

needs_approval_reason.description: Empty when no approval is needed.

post.summary: Re-derive the drawdown from the releases
post.description:
Always safe to run: the balance is recomputed from the release orders
rather than incremented, so this is also the repair for a blanket whose
figures were disturbed elsewhere.

Sets each blanket line's `released_qty`, and the blanket's
`released_amount`, `base_released_amount`, `remaining_amount` and
`release_count`. Rejected and cancelled releases add nothing to the
amounts, and are still counted in `release_count`. Needs `U` on
`purchase_order`.

Needs `R` on `vendor_price_agreement`. Rows are scoped by owner and

post.summary: Create a price agreement
post.description:
Requires `vendor_account_id` and one of `product_id` / `category_sku` —
without one the agreement covers nothing and the resolver would never
find it.

Needs `C` on `vendor_price_agreement`. `status` defaults to `active`,
and `agreement_number` is `VPA-NNNNNN`. With a `product_id`, `sku` and
`product_name` are copied from the product, and `category_sku` and
`uom` when they are blank. `price_break_list` entries that are not
numbers, or are negative, are dropped, and the rest are sorted by
`min_qty`.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `VENDOR_ACCOUNT_ID_REQUIRED` | no `vendor_account_id` |
| `INVALID_VENDOR_ACCOUNT_ID`, `VENDOR_ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND` | the account is malformed or not in the tenant |
| `PRODUCT_ID_OR_CATEGORY_SKU_REQUIRED` | neither is sent |
| `PRODUCT_NOT_FOUND` | `product_id` names no product in the tenant |
| `INVALID_STATUS` | `status` is not in the list |
| `UNIT_PRICE_NEGATIVE`, `UNIT_PRICE_NOT_A_NUMBER` | `unit_price` |
| `INVALID_VALIDITY_DATES`, `VALID_TO_BEFORE_VALID_FROM` | the dates |
| `INVALID_BOOKS_ENTITY_ID` | `books_entity_id` is not all digits |
| `SITE_CODE_NOT_REGISTERED` | `site_code` is not a site the tenant has registered. `data` is `{site_code}`. |

An account whose `relationship_type` is not `vendor` is accepted.

delete.description:
Needs `D` on `vendor_price_agreement`. Deletes the named agreements in
the tenant, whatever their status. No ids gives `INVALID_DATA`. A
malformed id gives `INVALID_VENDOR_PRICE_AGREEMENT_ID`.

Needs `R` on `vendor_price_agreement`. The stored document; its id is

patch.description:
**`vendor_account_id` and `product_id` are IMMUTABLE** and refused
explicitly (`IMMUTABLE_FIELD_<FIELD>`). Repointing an agreement is not
an edit, it is a different deal, and it would retroactively change the
meaning of every order line already citing this agreement id.

Also refused with `IMMUTABLE_FIELD_<FIELD>`: `vendor_price_agreement_id`,
`tenant_id`, `site_code`, `base_unit_price`, `created_by_userid`,
`timestamp` and `agreement_number`. Needs `U` on
`vendor_price_agreement`. `VENDOR_PRICE_AGREEMENT_NOT_FOUND` when the id
is not in the tenant. The create checks on `status`, `unit_price` and
the dates apply.

Delete removes an agreement whether or not orders cite it. Setting
`status` to `superseded` keeps it.

get.summary: What does this cost, and on whose authority
get.description:
**Always answers, and always names the basis.** A price shown without
its basis is one nobody can question later.

Precedence, most specific first:

| `basis` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `agreement_entity` | Vendor + product, scoped to this legal company |
| `agreement_group` | Vendor + product, group-wide (blank company) |
| `agreement_category` | Vendor + category |
| `product_purchase_cost` | The item master's recorded cost |
| `product_standard_cost` | The item master's estimate |
| `none` | Nothing found. The buyer types a price. |

`found: false` with `basis: none` is a **real answer**, not an error — a
404 here would make every unpriced line look like a broken request.

An expired agreement never prices a line. `status` alone does not prove
one is live: nothing sweeps agreements to `expired` when their window
closes, so both the status and the date window are checked.

`agreement_entity` is tried only when `books_entity_id` is sent. The
category tier uses the product's `category_sku` when none is sent. Among
matching agreements the latest `valid_from_date` wins. The price is the
highest quantity break that `qty` meets, else `unit_price`. When that is
zero and the agreement has `discount_pct`, the discount is taken off the
product's `purchase_cost`.

A quantity below the agreement's minimum is REPORTED
(`below_min_order_qty`), not refused.

Needs `R` on `vendor_price_agreement`. No `vendor_account_id` gives
`INVALID_DATA`. An unreadable `qty` is treated as 0. An unreadable
`on_date` means now.

Purchase orders in `approved` or `ordered`, sorted by `needed_by_date`
ascending. Blanket agreements are never listed. Scoped by the caller's
sites. The order's owner and `access_dict` play no part. A tenant admin, or a caller whose
roles carry no site code, sees every site. Needs `R` on `goods_receipt`.
No prices.

On the default sort, orders with no `needed_by_date` move to the end of
their page. In `match_filter_dict`, `vendor_account_id` is read as
`account_id`. `open_line_count` and `outstanding_qty` leave out
closed lines. An order with nothing left can still appear while its
stage is `approved` or `ordered`.

`match_filter_dict` and `sort_dict` narrow the list and can never widen
it: the filter is AND-ed with the dock's scope. Only fields a dock can see
are accepted. Anything else is refused with
`MATCH_FILTER_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED_<FIELD>`, `MATCH_FILTER_OPERATOR_NOT_ALLOWED_<OP>`
or `SORT_FIELD_NOT_ALLOWED_<FIELD>`, never silently dropped.

- Filter fields: `_id`, `site_code`, `account_id`, `stage`, `received_status`,
  `needed_by_date`, `expected_delivery_date`, `po_number`, `name`,
  `deliver_to_location_code`.
- Operators: `$in`, `$nin`, `$eq`, `$ne`, `$gt`, `$gte`, `$lt`, `$lte`, `$exists`.
  Values are scalars or lists of scalars.
- Sort fields: `needed_by_date`, `expected_delivery_date`, `po_number`, `name`,
  `site_code`, with 1 or -1.
- A malformed filter or sort gives `INVALID_MATCH_FILTER_DICT` or
  `INVALID_SORT_DICT`.

Orders as a dock reads them. A failed read is a failure

get.description:
A draft pre-filled with what is still outstanding on the order.
Somebody standing at a loading bay should confirm what arrived, not
retype an order.

Every line carries `ordered_qty`, `received_qty_to_date` (posted receipts
only, drafts are not counted), `closed_qty`,
`remaining_qty = max(0, ordered_qty - received_qty_to_date - closed_qty)`,
`uom`, `uom_precision` and `line_status`. `received_qty` is pre-filled
with `remaining_qty`. The figures come from the order's lines as last
rolled up.

Needs `R` on `goods_receipt`. Creates nothing, and does not check the
order's stage or type. `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND` when the id is not in
the tenant.

post.summary: Close short lines, or the whole order
post.description:
Stops expecting the rest of a line. Each closed line gets
`closed_qty += remaining_qty` through a `closed_short` event, and
`qty_on_order` at its site and product comes down by exactly that
remaining quantity. No `po_line_ids` closes every open line.

When every line is `received`, `over_received` or `closed`, the order's
stage becomes `received`. A purchase order has no `closed` stage.

Gated like posting a receipt: `D` on `goods_receipt`. A repeated
`client_request_id` returns the current sheet with `duplicate: true` and
writes nothing.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_RECEIVABLE` | the order is a blanket, or not approved, ordered, received or billed. The same code as creating a receipt. |
| `PO_LINE_NOT_FOUND` | a `po_line_ids` entry is not on the order (`data.po_line_id`) |
| `PO_LINE_ALREADY_CLOSED` | the line is closed (`data` has the line's figures) |
| `PO_LINE_NOTHING_REMAINING` | nothing is left to receive on the line, or on the order |
| `PO_CLOSE_REASON_REQUIRED` | `reason` is blank |
| `NOT_AUTHORIZED_FOR_GOODS_RECEIPT` | the caller cannot post receipts |

200.description: The receiving sheet after the close, plus `closed_po_line_ids`.

qty_on_order_change.description: How `qty_on_order` moved, per product and site. Signed; empty on a duplicate.

post.summary: Undo a close
post.description:
Writes a `reopened` event for the closed quantity, puts the remaining
back on order, and moves a `received` order back to the stage it came
from. No `po_line_ids` reopens every closed line that still has something
to receive.

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `PO_LINE_NOT_CLOSED` | the line is not closed |
| `PO_LINE_NOTHING_REMAINING` | a later receipt already brought everything, so reopening would change nothing |
| `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_RECEIVABLE`, `PO_LINE_NOT_FOUND`, `PO_CLOSE_REASON_REQUIRED` | as for close |

200.description: The receiving sheet after the reopen, plus `reopened_po_line_ids`.

qty_on_order_change.description: How `qty_on_order` moved, per product and site. Signed; empty on a duplicate.

Filter by `purchase_order_id` for the deliveries against one order.
Needs `R` on `goods_receipt`. Rows are scoped by owner and
`access_dict`. Each row is the stored header (id in `id`) with
`receipt_line_list`, `status`, `received_date` and `received_by` added.

post.summary: Record a delivery
post.description:
Opens in `draft`. **Nothing moves until it is posted.** Needs `C` on
`goods_receipt`. `receipt_number` is `GR-NNNNNN`.

Each receipt line is matched to an order line by `po_line_id`, or else
by `product_id`. A line that matches neither is refused with
`PO_LINE_NOT_FOUND`, and `data` has `{po_line_id, product_id}`. It is the
same code closing a line uses. A `rejection_reason` outside the list
gives `INVALID_REJECTION_REASON`.

`site_code` goes through the platform resolver: the body's value, else
the order's, else the receiver's only site. The vendor, currency, FX rate
and `books_entity_id` are copied from the order.

A line with a quantity on a CLOSED order line is refused with
`PO_LINE_CLOSED`, `data: {po_line_id}`. Reopen the line first.

An order that is not approved, ordered or received (a draft, pending
approval, rejected or cancelled order) is refused with
`PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_RECEIVABLE`, when the receipt is created and again
when it is posted. A missing or malformed
`purchase_order_id` gives `INVALID_PURCHASE_ORDER_ID`, and one not in
the tenant gives `PURCHASE_ORDER_NOT_FOUND`. A `site_code` the tenant
has not registered gives `SITE_CODE_NOT_REGISTERED`, with `data: {site_code}`.
This applies to a site copied from the order too.

Lines are priced from the ORDER, never from the delivery note.

**A blanket agreement cannot be received against**
(`CANNOT_RECEIVE_AGAINST_A_BLANKET`). Goods arrive against a release.

**Send `client_receipt_id` from any client that can retry.** A replay
returns the original receipt with `duplicate: true` and HTTP 200 rather
than creating a second one. See the field for why this matters more here
than almost anywhere else in the API. That holds when the original is
also the order's open draft.

**One open draft per order.** If the order already has a draft, that
draft is returned with `existing_draft: true` and the lines sent are not
applied. Edit it with `PATCH`.

Lines are stored one document each in `goods_receipt_line`;
`receipt_line_list` in every response is read from there.

A line over the over-delivery limit (`GET /user/inventory/settings`) is
saved, and reported in `warnings`. Posting it is refused.

200.description:
The delivery, in `draft`. `duplicate: true` means this key had
already been recorded and the receipt returned is the original —
a success, not a failure.

duplicate.description: Present and true only on a recognised replay.

existing_draft.description: Present and true when the order's open draft was returned instead.

get.description:
Needs `R` on `goods_receipt`. Scoped by owner and `access_dict`;
`NOT_FOUND` when the caller cannot see it. The stored header (id in
`id`) with `receipt_line_list`, `status`, `received_date` and
`received_by` added.

patch.description:
A posted or cancelled receipt is refused
(`RECEIPT_NOT_EDITABLE_IN_STAGE_<STAGE>`). Correct a posted one by
cancelling it. Needs `U` on `goods_receipt`.

`receipt_line_list` (or `lines`) replaces the draft's lines when it is a
list. Send a line's `line_id` (or `goods_receipt_line_id`) back to keep
its id, its `created_by_userid` and its `created_ts`. The response carries
`warnings` as on create. `received_date` is accepted in place of
`receipt_date`.

These keys are refused with `READ_ONLY_FIELD_<FIELD>`:
`goods_receipt_id`, `tenant_id`, `purchase_order_id`, `receipt_number`,
`stage`, `posted_ts`, `posted_by_userid`, `inventory_posted`,
`inventory_txn_ids`, `reversal_txn_ids`, `total_received_qty`,
`total_accepted_qty`, `total_rejected_qty`, `total_received_amount`,
`base_total_received_amount`, `line_count`, `lines_migrated_ts`.

Also refused: `PO_LINE_NOT_FOUND` and `PO_LINE_CLOSED`, as on create.
`GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTING_IN_PROGRESS` while another request posts or
cancels this receipt. `RECEIPT_POSTING_INCOMPLETE` when a post stopped
after stock moved: post it again to finish it.

post.summary: Post the receipt — stock moves
post.description:
**Gated on `D` for `goods_receipt`, not `U`.** Recording what turned up
is routine floor work; posting it moves stock, closes an order line and
lets a bill be paid.

Posting:

1. writes one stock movement per accepted line, carrying
   `source_entity_type: purchase_order`, `source_entity_id`,
   `source_line_id` (the order line), `goods_receipt_id`,
   `goods_receipt_line_id`, `po_number`, `po_line_number`,
   `receipt_number` and `reference` (the receipt number);
2. marks each line `posted`, snapshots `ordered_qty` and
   `received_qty_to_date_before`, and appends its events: `received`,
   then `accepted` and `rejected` when above zero, then
   `delivered_to_stock` when stock moved;
3. recomputes the order's per-line `received_qty` and `closed_qty`, its
   `received_status` and stage, and moves `qty_on_order` by exactly the
   drop in the order's remaining quantity;
4. adds the accepted quantity to `received_qty` on the requisition line
   the order line came from.

Each post also stamps the order's `received_date` when it is unset, and
asks the installed-base service to provision records for the order lines
that arrived.

**Idempotent**: posting an already-posted receipt returns it with
`already: true` rather than moving stock twice. A double-tap on a
loading bay is a tap, not a decision.

**One post at a time.** A second post of the same receipt waits for the
first. It answers `already: true` when the first finished, or
`GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTING_IN_PROGRESS` after 15 seconds; try again. Each
stock movement carries a `client_txn_id` made from its receipt line, so
a post that stopped part way and is posted again moves the stock once.

Refused when nothing was accepted (`RECEIPT_HAS_NOTHING_ACCEPTED`).
Refused with `PO_LINE_CLOSED` (`data: {po_line_id}`) when a line was
closed after the draft was counted. Reopen the line, then post.
Also refused:

| error_code | When |
|---|---|
| `RECEIPT_IS_CANCELLED` | the receipt is cancelled |
| `RECEIPT_SITE_REQUIRED` | the tenant has more than one site and an accepted line has no site |
| an Inventory place code | a stocked line's site, location or bin is not set up |
| `RECEIPT_MOVED_NO_STOCK` | every stocked line's movement failed. The receipt stays a draft. |
| `GOODS_RECEIPT_NOT_FOUND`, `INVALID_GOODS_RECEIPT_ID` | the id |

A line with no `product_id` moves no stock. When some stocked lines
move and others fail, the receipt still posts.

**Over-delivery limit.** Refused with `GOODS_RECEIPT_OVER_TOLERANCE` when
a line's `received_qty_to_date` plus this receipt's quantity exceeds
`ordered_qty * (1 + over_receipt_tolerance_pct / 100)`. The tolerance
defaults to 10. `data`:
`{po_line_id, ordered_qty, received_qty_to_date, received_qty,
allowed_qty, allowed_total_qty, tolerance_pct}`; `allowed_qty` is how much
this delivery may still add, `allowed_total_qty` the line's limit across
every receipt. The quantity compared is the one taken into stock
(`accepted_qty`), the same measure as `received_qty_to_date`. At exactly
the limit it posts. A line received past its ordered quantity is
`over_received`. Nothing moves when refused.

posted.description: 1 when this request posted it. 0 with `already`.

post.summary: Reverse a posted receipt, or cancel a draft
post.description:
**Never deletes and never edits what was written.** Cancelling posts
OFFSETTING movements, built from the movements this receipt actually
wrote, so it unwinds exactly what happened. What was reversed goes back
on order, by exactly the rise in the order's remaining quantity.

Each posted line becomes `cancelled` (with `reversal_txn_id`) and gets a
`cancelled` event naming the offsetting transaction. Nothing else on the
line changes.

A reversal is recorded as an ISSUE, not a negative receipt.

A draft can be cancelled too: its lines become `cancelled` and no stock
moves. Needs `D` on `goods_receipt`. A `reason` is appended to `notes`.
Cancelling a cancelled receipt returns it with `already: true`.

One cancel at a time, like posting: a second request answers
`already: true` or `GOODS_RECEIPT_POSTING_IN_PROGRESS`. A draft whose
post stopped after stock moved is refused with
`RECEIPT_POSTING_INCOMPLETE`: post it to finish, then cancel.

get.description:
Ordered vs received vs billed, line by line.

**Reports the variance; does NOT block the bill.** Whether a variance
stops a payment is a tenant policy, and a hard block here would strand a
payables clerk with no way forward.

Billed figures come from the Bill named by the order's `bill_id`, whose
lines are matched to order lines by position. A line is `over_billed`
when billed exceeds received, and `qty_variance` when received differs
from ordered. It is `price_variance` when the billed unit price differs
from the order's by more than 0.5%, unless it is already `over_billed`.
The order's `match_status` is the worst line, or `not_matched` when the
order has no lines. Needs `R` on `goods_receipt`. Writes nothing.

200.description: The comparison, at the top level of the envelope.

post.summary: Award an RFP to one supplier
post.description:
Records which response won, then creates the **contract** and the
**purchase order**.

**Where this sits.** The sequence is: a requisition is raised and
APPROVED against budget, its value crosses a threshold so an RFP is
required, bids come back, one is awarded, a contract is signed, and a
PO is issued against the requisition.

**This never creates a requisition.** A requisition is the
authorisation to spend, obtained before anyone approaches the market.
Creating one here would ask an approver to bless a price already agreed
with a supplier who had already won, and would let an RFP go out against
no budget at all. An RFP with no approved requisition is REFUSED.

**The award is written before the documents it creates**, and there is
no transaction across them. An awarded RFP whose contract failed is
visible on the RFP and can be completed; a contract with no award behind
it is invisible. `failed` names every step that did not complete, so a
caller retries without re-awarding.

**The vendor is validated here.** It lives on the share LINK, never on
the questionnaire, and `recipient.account_id` is a free-form field never
checked against `relationship_type` at share time.

Needs `C` on `purchase_order`. Also subject to the Pro gate.

response_id.description: The winning response. Must belong to this RFP or to one of its share instances; anything else is refused.

contract_template_id.description: The template the contract is built from.

deal_type.description: A term deal opens a BLANKET order whose releases draw against it. A one-off opens a standard order.

awarded_amount.description: Carries the FX block, like every amount here.

200.description: What was created, and what was not. HTTP 200 either way; the envelope carries the detail, as everywhere else in this module.

purchase_requisition_id.description: Reported, never created. It authorised this spend before the RFP went out.

failed.description: Steps that did not complete. Empty on a clean award.

422.description:
Refused, in the standard envelope with `result: 2`.

`RFP_NOT_SOURCING` — not an RFP.
`RFP_RESPONSE_NOT_FOUND` — the response is not on this RFP.
`RFP_ALREADY_AWARDED` — revoke first.
`RFP_RECIPIENT_NOT_VENDOR` — the supplier is not a vendor account.
`RFP_CONTRACT_TEMPLATE_REQUIRED` — no template chosen.
`RFP_DEAL_TYPE_INVALID` — deal_type is neither one_off nor term.
`RFP_REQUISITION_REQUIRED` — no requisition authorised this spend.
`RFP_REQUISITION_NOT_APPROVED` — one exists but has not cleared its chain.

delete.description:
Clears the award and cancels the documents it opened.

**Refuses once the decision has left the building.** A contract in
`sending`, `sent`, `signed` or `completed` has been seen by somebody
outside the tenant; an order in `approved` or later is a commitment
somebody made deliberately. Either refuses with `RFP_AWARD_LOCKED`.

**The requisition is never cancelled.** It carries demand somebody
asked for, which outlives the decision about who supplies it, and it is
what a second RFP would be raised from.

Shipped with the award on purpose: an award that can only be made is a
decision nobody can correct, and the correction people reach for
otherwise is editing the contract and the order by hand.

parameters.name: questionnaire_id
parameters.description: The RFP. Sending it in a DELETE body still works for one release and is deprecated.

422.description:
`RFP_AWARD_NOT_FOUND` — nothing to revoke.
`RFP_AWARD_LOCKED` — the contract is sent or the order approved.
`RFP_NOT_SOURCING` — not an RFP.

PageSize.name: page_size
PageSize.description: Rows per page. Above 500 is treated as 500.

SortDict.name: sort_dict
SortDict.description: JSON-encoded, e.g. `{"needed_by_date": 1}`. A GET has no body.

IdsList.name: ids_list
IdsList.description:
JSON array of ids. **ANDed onto `match_filter_dict`, never merged** — a
merge would drop one of two id clauses and answer "these three rows"
with the whole collection.

IdsListRequired.name: ids_list
IdsListRequired.description:
JSON array of ids. A single bare id is accepted. Also read from
`<entity>_ids` or `<entity>_ids_list`, for example
`purchase_requisition_ids`.

GetCount.name: get_count
GetCount.description:
`true`, `1`, `yes` or `on`. On page 1 it returns `total_count` with no
rows. It has no effect on later pages.

ListId.name: list_id
ListId.description:
A saved list to apply: its static ids, or its dynamic filter. The list
must be the caller's own or a global one. An unknown id is ignored.

Envelope.description:
The platform envelope. Success and refusal are HTTP 200; branch on
`result`. A missing token is HTTP 401 with no body.

error_code.description:
Present when `result` is 2. Stable, safe to branch on.
`PROCUREMENT_READ_FAILED` means the read failed. It is never sent for
an empty result.

data.description: Present on some refusals, with the details named in the operation.

ApprovalDecisionResult.description: Fields an approval decision adds to the record it returns.

already.description: The record was already decided and nothing was written.

acted_step_seq.description: Sequenced chains only. The step the caller acted on.

next_approval_seq.description: Sequenced chains only. The step now pending, `0` when none.

steps_remaining.description: Sequenced chains only. Steps still pending.

billed_unit_price.description: Null when the bill does not price the line.

RequisitionStage.description:
`partially_ordered`, `ordered` and `closed` are DERIVED from the lines
and are never set by a client. `closed` means some line was closed short
— the requester did not get everything they asked for.

purchase_requisition_id.description: On create and update responses. Reads carry only `id`.

id.description: The record id. On reads, and copied onto create and update responses.

justification.description: Why it is needed. The first thing an approver reads.

department_code.description: A reporting tag. Not an access code.

suggested_vendor_account_id.description: The requester's suggestion, not a commitment.

site_code.description: Set at create. Refused on update.

estimated_total.description: An estimate. Not an agreed price.

approval_threshold_label.description: Which amount band routed this request, kept so an approval stays explainable after the table changes.

needed_by_date.description: Epoch seconds, or a date string. Stored as midnight in the tenant's time zone.

line_list.description: Replaces the lines wholesale on an update. Also accepted as `lines`. Each line takes the header's `needed_by_date`, `site_code` (as `deliver_to_site_code`), `expense_account_id`, `suggested_vendor_account_id`, `currency` and `fx_rate` unless it sends its own.

site_code.description: Resolved through the platform resolver. Blank falls back to the creator's only site.

purchase_requisition_line_id.description: On serialized responses (update, close short, the work list). Reads carry only `id`.

id.description: The record id. On reads, and copied onto serialized responses.

requisition_stage.description: The request's stage, copied onto the line. An approval decision writes it onto every line of the request.

product_id.description: Optional. A free-text ask is legitimate.

open_qty.description:
`max(0, qty - ordered_qty)`, denormalised. `0` once closed short.
Roll-up; REFUSED on write.

remaining_qty.description: max(0, qty - ordered_qty). Serialized responses only.

is_buyer_actionable.description:
Derived: the request is `approved` or `partially_ordered`, the line
is `open` or `partially_ordered`, and something is unordered. This
is what the work list filters on.

deliver_to_site_code.description:
Where the goods must arrive. Separate from `site_code`, which is the
access-control partition — a central buyer raises orders that
deliver to a branch.

RequisitionLineWrite.description:
A line needs `product_id` or `description`, and a `qty` above 0. With a
`product_id`, `sku` is copied from the product, and `product_name`,
`category_sku` and `uom` when they are blank. `estimated_amount`,
`base_estimated_amount`, `open_qty` and `status` are computed.

inventory_item_id_list.description:
The stock rows to order against. Capped at 500 — a reorder run is a
person ticking rows, and one mis-click should not raise a
requisition nobody can usefully approve or reject.

needed_by_date.description: Epoch. Applied to the header and to every line.

books_entity_id.description: The legal company. Also scopes which price agreements apply.

stage.description:
The stage each order is created in. `draft` or `pending_approval`
are the intended values. Any purchase order stage is accepted. Any
other value fails with `PURCHASE_ORDER_STAGE_INVALID`.
`pending_approval` builds the order's approval chain.

price_on_date.description: Epoch. Which day's price agreements apply. Defaults to now.

vendor_price_agreement_id.description: On create and update responses. Reads carry only `id`.

id.description: The record id. On reads, and copied onto create and update responses.

vendor_account_id.description: Immutable. An account in the tenant.

product_id.description: Immutable. Empty means a category agreement.

price_break_list.description:
Ascending by `min_qty`. The HIGHEST break the order quantity meets
wins; below every break the headline `unit_price` applies.

discount_pct.description: An alternative expression, applied to the product's recorded purchase cost.

books_entity_id.description: Create only. All digits, or blank.

sku.description: Create only. Replaced from the product when `product_id` is set.

product_name.description: Create only. Replaced from the product when `product_id` is set.

below_min_order_qty.description: True when the agreement has a `min_order_qty` and `qty` is below it. The price is still returned.

goods_receipt_id.description: On create, update, post and cancel responses. Reads carry only `id`.

id.description: The record id. On reads, and copied onto create, update, post and cancel responses.

client_receipt_id.description: Blank for a receipt sent without one.

received_by.description: Same as `userid`: who took the delivery.

inventory_txn_ids.description: The stock movements posting wrote. A cancellation reverses exactly these.

allowed_qty.description: What this delivery may still add.

allowed_total_qty.description: The line's limit across every receipt: ordered_qty * (1 + pct / 100).

GoodsReceiptEvent.description:
One thing that happened to a received line, or to an order line for
`closed_short` and `reopened` (`goods_receipt_line_id` is empty there).
Append-only. `migrated: true` marks events copied from a receipt written
before lines had their own collection.

event_key.description: Idempotency key: the same event is never written twice.

client_receipt_id.description:
**Idempotency key. Send one from any client that can retry.**

A tablet on a loading bay sends a receipt, the response is lost, and
the retry is indistinguishable from a second delivery. Without a
key, replaying writes TWO receipts against one pallet — post both
and the stock doubles, the order line closes on twice what arrived,
and a bill becomes payable for it. Nothing errors.

A replay returns the ORIGINAL receipt with `duplicate: true` and
HTTP 200, not an error: a retrying client should see the answer it
missed rather than something it has to interpret.

Generate it once per delivery and reuse it across retries. A key
minted per attempt is not a key. Omit it entirely for a receipt
typed on a screen.

receipt_line_list.description: Also accepted as `lines`. Each line takes `po_line_id` (or `product_id`), `received_qty`, `accepted_qty`, `rejected_qty`, `rejection_reason`, the place codes, `lot_number`, `serial_number` and `expiry_date`.

GoodsReceiptUpdate.description: The editable fields of a draft. Keys not listed here are ignored, except the refused ones named on the operation.

site_code.description: Stored as sent. The site resolver is not applied.

receipt_line_list.description: Replaces the draft's lines. Also accepted as `lines`.

ReceiptLine.description:
**Received, accepted and rejected are three different numbers.** Only
the accepted quantity moves stock and satisfies the order.

unit_price.description: From the ORDER, never from the delivery note. Ignored on write.

accepted_qty.description:
What was taken into stock. **Defaults to what arrived**, less
anything explicitly rejected. Capped at `received_qty`.

rejected_qty.description: What went back on the van.

tracking_mode.description: Whether the item needs a lot or a serial number on receipt. Empty when it needs neither.

reject_reason.description: Same as `rejection_reason`. Either spelling is accepted on write.

site_code.description: Same as `to_site_code`. Either spelling is accepted on write.

location_code.description: Same as `to_location_code`. Either spelling is accepted on write.

bin_code.description: Same as `to_bin_code`. Either spelling is accepted on write.

created_by_userid.description: Who first entered the line. Returned on reads. Editing a draft's lines keeps it, together with `created_ts`.

created_ts.description: When the line was first entered. Kept when a draft is edited.

cancelled_by_userid.description: Who cancelled the line. On a line copied from an older receipt (`migrated: true`) it is the person named on the receipt's `cancelled` event.

received_qty_to_date.description: Where the PO line stands now: accepted on posted receipts.
